Short answer: yes. I'm attaching a first-pass PDF snapshot and a one-paragraph narrative tailored for SOC 2. The PDF contains two panels (Dedicated vs Private) and highlights:

- Control plane endpoints (management API, metrics/ops) on an isolated control VPC with mTLS and restricted peering.

Tom / Marissa — added some technical notes below that will map to CAIQ answers. I'm pasting the short checklist items first, then a few clarifiers.

Checklist (short answers):
- Control plane separation: YES (separate VPCs with peering over private links; management plane authenticated via mutual TLS and tenant-scoped RBAC).
- Data plane tenant isolation: YES (per-tenant runtime namespaces, encrypted at-rest, no shared KV for customer secrets).
- KV cache / model cache handling: Caches are local to the GPU node group; eviction and zeroization on instance tear-down; logs scrubbed of sensitive content.
- Egress controls: YES (default deny egress for Private; Dedicated has managed egress proxies with allowlist; customers can provide CIDR ranges).

Clarifiers / implementation bullets:
- For Dedicated, we operate a management cluster in a separate control VPC in the same region; customer traffic routes to dedicated inference pools via service endpoints (no internet hairpin).
- Private (VPC) deployments run the same runtime but with customer-managed networking; KMS integrations keep keys in the customer's KMS/HSM when requested.
- Control-plane telemetry uses an outbound-only collector that ships to our metrics namespace; audit logs are immutable and retained per contract.

I'll attach a more granular controlplane-egress-matrix.xlsx with the egress categories and example CIDRs. Ben, final VSDX please.

—Kimberly Park
Senior Security Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: controlplane-egress-matrix.xlsx

Tom — confirmed for Thu 22 Oct 15:00 PT (calendar invite sent). Attached is the final package and short SOC 2 snippet you can paste into your evidence binder. Below are the quick CAIQ-style bullets you asked for; I also added a shared Drive folder with the VSDX/PDF and the egress matrix.

SOC 2 narrative (paste-ready):
"Redwood Inference enforces a strict separation between the management/control plane and customer data-plane for both Dedicated and Private deployments. The control plane — which handles orchestration, metrics, and billing — is hosted in an isolated management VPC with mTLS authentication, tenant-scoped RBAC, and restricted peering. Customer inference workloads run in segregated runtime namespaces with encrypted-at-rest storage and outbound egress policy enforcement; no customer model artifacts or secrets are stored in the control plane. Regular audits and immutable audit logs are retained per contract."

CAIQ-style bullets (network):
- Network egress filtering: Yes — default deny for Private deployments; Dedicated uses managed egress proxies with an allowlist. Exceptions granted via CIDR list and recorded in the egress matrix.
- Control-plane access: Mutual TLS + tenant-scoped service accounts; admin operations over private links only.
- Tenant isolation: Per-tenant runtime namespaces, separate storage buckets, and encrypted caches; KV caches are ephemeral and zeroized on tear-down.
- Auditability: All access and admin events are logged to immutable audit streams; logs retained per contract.
